summary: When a notified disease (listed under the Third Schedule of the Code) occurs in an establishment, the employer, occupier, or manager must immediately send a Notice of Disease electronically to the Inspector Cum Facilitator or Chief Inspector Cum Facilitator.

If a person injured in an accident or dangerous occurrence (already reported) subsequently dies, the employer/occupier/manager must immediately notify the relevant authorities by telephone and electronically, and confirm the information in writing within 12 hours of the death.

source_refs.citation_span: page:9 / proviso — forthwith by telephone and electronically, confirmed in writing within 12 hours of death

summary: If a worker's disability from an accident or dangerous occurrence reaches 48 hours or more but does not arise immediately (or occurs in multiple spells), the employer/occupier/manager must send the prescribed report to the Inspector-cum-Facilitator within 24 hours of the cumulative disability total reaching 48 hours.

source_refs.citation_span: page:9 / proviso further — report within 24 hours after cumulative disability becomes 48 hours

summary: When a dangerous occurrence (as specified in the annexed table) takes place in an establishment, the employer/occupier/manager must send a notice in Form-VIII to the Inspector-cum-Facilitator and the District Magistrate or Sub-Divisional Officer within 12 hours, regardless of whether bodily injury or disability resulted.
proof_types: acknowledgment of receipt by District Magistrate/SDO

source_refs.citation_span: page:9 / dangerous occurrence notice — Form-VIII within twelve hours

summary: Where more than one Safety Officer is appointed in a factory, designate the most senior among them as the Chief Safety Officer, who shall hold a higher status and have overall supervisory responsibility over the other Safety Officers.
Ensure no worker is required or allowed to work more than 48 hours in any week in an establishment.

Arrange work periods so that, inclusive of rest intervals, a worker's working day does not spread over more than 10.5 hours (extendable to 12 hours with State Government notification and worker's written consent).

Post a notice in a conspicuous place outside the office of every establishment, in Kannada and English (or a language understood by the majority of workers), showing the weekly day of rest for each worker, relay, or set of persons.

Before requiring any adult worker to work on their weekly day of rest, the employer must deliver a prior notice to the office of the Inspector-cum-facilitator stating the intention to require work on that day and specifying the substituted holiday day.
Before requiring any adult worker to work on their weekly day of rest, the employer must display a notice to that effect within the establishment, identifying the substituted holiday.

If a previously issued notice requiring a worker to work on their weekly rest day is to be cancelled, deliver a cancellation notice to the Inspector-cum-facilitator's office AND display a cancellation notice in the establishment, both no later than the day before the rest day or the holiday to be cancelled (whichever is earlier).

The employer must display a notice, on or before the end of the month in which holidays are lost, listing workers granted compensatory holidays in the following month and the dates thereof, at the same location where the notice of periods of work under Section 26 is posted. Any subsequent changes to this notice must be made at least three days before the date of the compensatory holiday.

deadline_rule.event: end of month in which holidays are lost

summary: The employer must ensure that all compensatory holidays owed to a worker are granted before the worker is discharged or dismissed, and such holidays must not be counted as part of any notice period required before discharge or dismissal.

The employer must pay overtime wages at twice the ordinary rate of wages to any worker who works beyond the prescribed daily or weekly hour limits (more than 9 hours/day or 48 hours/week for a 6-day week; more than 10 hours/day or 48 hours/week for a 5-day week; more than 11.5 hours/day for a 4-day week; or works on paid holidays).

When calculating overtime for any day, the employer must count any fraction of an hour between 15 and 30 minutes as 30 minutes, and any fraction exceeding 30 minutes as a full hour, and maintain accurate overtime records on this basis.

Obtain prior approval from the Inspector-cum-Facilitator before employing an adult worker in more than one factory on the same day. Ensure the worker does not work more than eight hours in total across all factories on that day.

source_refs.citation_span: page:23 / r.33 'Restriction of double employment.- An adult worker may be employed, in more than one factory on the same day, with the previous approval of the Inspector-cum-Facilitator'

summary: Display the notice of periods of work in Form-XI at conspicuous places on a notice board or electronic board in Kannada and either in English or a language understood by the majority of employees. Send a copy of the notice to the Inspector-cum-Facilitator electronically or by registered post.
proof_types: Form-XI notice displayed on notice board
copy sent to Inspector-cum-Facilitator by registered post or electronically

summary: Maintain a register of workers, overtime work, fines, and deductions for damage or loss in Form-XII electronically. Keep the register available at an office or the nearest convenient building within the precincts of the establishment.

Where manual registers and records are maintained, enter all particulars legibly in ink in Kannada and either in English or the majority language, and preserve the originals for three calendar years after the date of the last report or entry. If the original is lost or destroyed before one year, preserve true copies for the prescribed period.
proof_types: true copies (if original lost or destroyed)

summary: Produce all registers and records electronically or by registered post before the Chief Inspector-cum-Facilitator on demand.
proof_types: registers submitted electronically or by registered post

summary: Every employer must display a notice at a conspicuous place in the workplace showing the establishment's name and address, hours of work, wage period, date of wage payment, details of accidents and dangerous occurrences for the last five years, name and address of the Inspector-cum-Facilitator, and date of payment of unpaid wages — in Kannada and either English or the language understood by the majority of workers.

Every employer must electronically submit an annual return for their establishment in Form-XIII to the Inspector-cum-Facilitator having jurisdiction, so that it is received no later than 1st February following the end of each calendar year.
Every employer must maintain a register of accidents and dangerous occurrences as required under section 33(a)(v) of the Code, in Form-XIV.
Every employer must maintain a record of leave with wages for each employee, either electronically or manually, in Form-XV.
The Form-XV leave with wages register must be preserved for at least three years after the last entry and must not be destroyed after that period unless properly transferred to a new register.

Every employer in factories, construction, beedi/cigar, plantation, or motor transport must arrange a free annual medical examination (using Form-V) for every worker aged 40 years or above, within 120 days from the start of each calendar year. The employer must obtain the Medical Certificate from the qualified medical practitioner and provide a copy to the employee.
proof_types: Medical Certificate from qualified medical practitioner
copy of medical certificate provided to employee

source_refs.citation_span: page:8 / r.5 (Annual Health Examination under Section 6(1)(c))

summary: Every employer must issue a letter of appointment in Form-VI to each employee before employing them. Existing employees who have not yet received an appointment letter must be issued one within three months of this rule coming into force.

source_refs.citation_span: page:8 / r.6(1) (Letter of appointment under Section 6(1)(f))

summary: Every employer must issue an experience certificate in Form-VII to each employee within seven days of that employee's cessation of employment.

When a fatal accident occurs at an establishment (factory, construction, plantation, beedi/cigar, or any other establishment), the employer must immediately notify by telephone the Inspector-cum-Facilitator, Chief Inspector-cum-Facilitator, District Magistrate/Sub-Divisional Officer, nearest police station, and the family/kin of the deceased, and also send a formal notice in Form-VIII electronically within 12 hours of the accident.

source_refs.citation_span: page:8 / r.7(1) (Notice of accidents and dangerous occurrence under Section 10(1))

summary: When an accident at an establishment causes bodily injury preventing a worker from working for 48 hours or more, the employer/occupier/manager must send a notice in Form-VIII electronically to the Inspector-cum-Facilitator within 12 hours after the completion of those 48 hours.

source_refs.citation_span: page:8 / r.7(2) (Notice of accidents and dangerous occurrence under Section 10(1))

summary: Hold Safety Committee meetings at least once every three months. Meetings may be held more frequently if necessary.
Record the minutes of every Safety Committee meeting and produce them before the Inspector Cum Facilitator on demand.

If the registration application was not submitted within the mandatory 60-day window, submit it with a late fee: 10% of the base fee for delays up to 30 days, 20% for delays up to 60 days, and 40% for delays beyond 60 days.

source_refs.citation_span: page:6 / sub-rule (3) Table for late fee

summary: Display a copy of the certificate of registration (Form-II) at a conspicuous place in the establishment premises, either as a hard copy or electronically.

Every registration application must be accompanied by an undertaking in Annexure-A on the company's letterhead, duly signed by the employer, occupier, or owner, declaring non-engagement of contract labourers in core activities, and uploaded on the portal.
proof_types: Signed undertaking in Annexure-A uploaded on labouronline.karnataka.gov.in

summary: Every online registration application must be accompanied by a Self-Declaration in Annexure-B and a Self-Declaration for Self Attestation in Annexure-C, submitted through the portal.
proof_types: Self-Declaration for Self Attestation in Annexure-C

summary: An employer of an establishment (including motor transport undertaking, newspaper establishment, audio-video production, building and other construction work, plantation, or other commercial establishment) with ten or more workers must submit an application for registration in Form I-A electronically via labouronline.karnataka.gov.in to the registering officer under the Labour Commissionerate, along with the prescribed fee based on employee count.
proof_types: Undertaking in Annexure-A on company letterhead
Self-Declaration for Self Attestation in Annexure-C

summary: Appoint the required number of Safety Officers for factories carrying on hazardous processes: one Safety Officer for 250–500 workers, and one Safety Officer for every 500 workers when employment is 501 or above.

Appoint the required number of Safety Officers for building or other construction work: one Safety Officer for 250–500 workers, and one Safety Officer for every 500 workers when employment is 501 or above.
Appoint the required number of Safety Officers for dock work: one Safety Officer for 500–1000 workers, and one Safety Officer for every 1000 workers when employment is 1001 or above.

An employee already in employment on the date of commencement of these rules must submit a gratuity nomination in Form I (in duplicate) to the employer within 90 days from the date of commencement of the rules.

An employee who completes one year of service after the date of commencement of these rules must submit a gratuity nomination in Form I (in duplicate) to the employer within 30 days of the completion of one year of service.

Within 30 days of receiving a nomination in Form I, the employer must verify the employee's service particulars against establishment records, return the duly attested duplicate copy to the employee with a receipt, and retain the original copy in the establishment.
An employee who has no family at the time of making a nomination must submit a fresh nomination in Form I (in duplicate) to the employer within 90 days of acquiring a family.

An employee, nominee, or their authorised representative must apply for gratuity in Form II to the employer, ordinarily within 30 days from the date gratuity became payable; where the date of superannuation or retirement is known, the application may be submitted up to 30 days before that date.

A claimant employee, nominee, or legal heir must apply in Form-IV to the competent authority within 180 days of the occurrence of the cause for the application, submitting as many extra copies as there are opposite parties.
The application under Rule 14(1) and all supporting documents must be submitted to the competent authority either in person, by registered post with acknowledgement due, or electronically.

Any person acting as an authorised representative on behalf of an employer or employee must present a letter of authority and a written statement to the competent authority explaining their interest and seeking permission to act.
Maintain a notice book in Form VIII in all establishments where 500 or more workmen are employed, as required under section 82(4) of the Code.
The employer must display a copy of the registration certificate at a conspicuous place on the premises where work is being carried out.
The employer must quote the registration number on all documents prepared or submitted by them in all correspondence with the relevant offices under the Code, schemes, rules, or regulations.
The employer must update any change in the details submitted in the form on the designated portal within thirty days of such change occurring.

Before applying for cancellation of registration, the employer must have filed all returns, paid all dues under the Code, and submitted a self-declaration certificate to that effect along with the cancellation application. The authority must decide on the cancellation application within ninety days of receipt of a complete application.

Display the notice referred to under Section 19(2) of the Code on Wages at prominent places in the workplace premises (where employment is carried on), in Hindi, English, and the local language, in physical or electronic form, so that every concerned employee can easily read its contents. A copy of the notice must also be sent electronically or by registered post to the Inspector-cum-Facilitator having jurisdiction.

To obtain approval for imposing a fine (as referred to in Rule 14), the employer must send detailed particulars specified therein to the Deputy Chief Labour Commissioner (Central) having jurisdiction, electronically or in writing. The authority must dispose of the matter within 30 days of receiving the notice, failing which it is deemed approved.

Whenever the employer makes any deduction under Section 20(2) of the Code on Wages, the employer must notify the Inspector-cum-Facilitator having jurisdiction electronically or in writing, clearly stating the reasons for the deduction, within 10 days of the date of such deduction.

Before deducting wages for loss or damage caused by an employee, the employer must give the employee a detailed written notice specifying the nature of the loss/damage and how the employee's negligence or default contributed to it, and must also give the employee an opportunity to explain. If a deduction is then made, the employer must notify the employee of the deduction within 15 days of the date of deduction.

source_refs.citation_span: page:11 / rule 18 (धारा 21 की उप-धारा (2) के अंतर्गत कटौती की प्रक्रिया)

summary: When recovering advances given to an employee (advance on commencement of employment or advance against unearned wages), the employer must recover them in instalments not exceeding 50% of wages in any wage period (subject to the ceiling in Rule 13), and must record the details of such recovery in the register maintained in Form-IV.

source_refs.citation_span: page:11 / rule 19 (धारा 23 के अंतर्गत अधिम वसूली के संबंध में शर्तें)

summary: Revise the variable dearness allowance (VDA) payable to employees with respect to minimum wages twice a year — once before 1 April and once before 1 October — based on the average Consumer Price Index for industrial workers published by the Labour Bureau, Ministry of Labour & Employment, Government of India, accounting for the cost of living and concession values for subsidised essential commodities.

source_refs.citation_span: page:6 / Rule 5 – पररवती मंहगाई भत्ते के पुनरीक्षण के लिए समय-अंतराल

summary: Notify employees of the designated weekly rest day(s) and any subsequent changes to those rest days by prominently displaying a notice at a specific location at the workplace before the change takes effect.

source_refs.citation_span: page:6 / Rule 7(1) – चौथा परंतुक: नोटिस के प्रदर्शन द्वारा सूचित किया जाएगा

summary: Where an employee performs two or more classes of work with different minimum wage rates, the employer must pay wages at not less than the applicable minimum rate for the time spent on each class of work respectively.
Where an employee is engaged on piece work for which only a minimum time rate (not a minimum piece rate) has been fixed, the employer must pay wages at not less than that minimum time rate.
Where an employee works on a designated rest day, the employer must pay wages at a rate not less than the overtime rate.
Where an employee works beyond the normal working day hours, the employer must pay overtime wages at not less than twice the normal rate of wages for every hour or part of an hour worked in excess.
All wages must be paid in current coin, currency notes, cheque, bank account credit, or electronic mode.
Employers must pay wages to daily-basis employees at the end of each shift.
Employers must pay wages to weekly-basis employees on the last working day of the week, before the weekly holiday.
Employers must pay wages to fortnightly-basis employees before the end of the second day after the close of the fortnight.
Employers must pay wages to monthly-basis employees before the expiry of the seventh day of the succeeding month.
Employers must pay all outstanding wages to an employee within two working days of their removal, dismissal, retrenchment, resignation, or unemployment due to establishment closure.
Employers must ensure that no deductions are made from an employee's wages except those explicitly authorised under the Code on Wages. Maintain documentation justifying any deductions made.
The employer must ensure that total deductions from an employee's wages in any wage period do not exceed fifty per cent of such wages.

Before imposing a fine on any employee, the employer must obtain prior approval from the appropriate Government or prescribed authority specifying the acts and omissions for which fines may be imposed.
The employer must display a notice on the workplace premises specifying the acts and omissions for which fines may be imposed on employees, in the manner prescribed.
Before imposing a fine, the employer must give the employee an opportunity to show cause against the fine and follow the prescribed procedure for imposition of fines.
The employer must recover any fine imposed on an employee in a single payment and must not recover it by instalments or after ninety days from the date it was imposed.

The employer must maintain a register recording all fines imposed and all realisations thereof, in the manner and form prescribed, and ensure all realisations are applied only to purposes beneficial to employees as approved by the prescribed authority.
Before making any wage deduction for damage or loss caused by an employee, give the employee an opportunity to show cause against the proposed deduction and follow the prescribed procedure.
Maintain a register recording all deductions made from employee wages for damage or loss, and all realisations thereof, in the prescribed form.

If an employee has not worked all working days in an accounting year, the employer must proportionately reduce the minimum bonus (under s.26(1)) relative to the days actually worked, but only if the full minimum bonus would exceed 8⅓% of wages for days worked.

Employers must disqualify and withhold bonus from any employee dismissed for fraud, riotous or violent behaviour on premises, theft/misappropriation/sabotage of establishment property, or conviction for sexual harassment.

Ensure no discrimination exists among employees on the ground of gender in matters relating to wages for the same work or work of a similar nature. The employer must maintain equal wages across all genders for equivalent work.
Do not reduce the rate of wages of any employee as a means of complying with the equal-wages requirement under section 3(1).

source_refs.citation_span: s.3(2)(i) – 'for the purposes of complying with the provisions of sub-section (1), reduce the rate of wages of any employee'

summary: Do not discriminate on the ground of sex while recruiting any employee for the same work or work of similar nature, and in the conditions of employment, except where employment of women is prohibited or restricted by law.

source_refs.citation_span: s.3(2)(ii) – 'make any discrimination on the ground of sex while recruiting any employee for the same work or work of similar nature and in the conditions of employment, except where the employment of women in such work is prohibited or restricted by or under any law for the time being in force.'

summary: When computing bonus, employers must treat all departments, undertakings, and branches of an establishment as a single establishment, unless a separate balance sheet and profit & loss account are prepared and maintained for a department/branch for that accounting year (in which case it may be treated as a separate establishment).
Employers must pay bonus out of allocable surplus, calculated as 60% of available surplus for banking companies or 67% for all other establishments, with available surplus computed per section 33.
An employer must pay every employee wages that are not less than the minimum rate of wages notified by the appropriate Government. Paying below the notified minimum wage is prohibited.
Any settlement reached during conciliation proceedings or through any other means between employer and employee must be recorded in writing using Form I.

Every settlement memorandum must be signed by the employer (or authorised agent/principal officer) and on behalf of workers by specified trade union office-bearers or duly authorised worker representatives.

Where a settlement is reached outside conciliation proceedings, the parties to the settlement must jointly send a copy electronically or by speed post or registered post to the Deputy Chief Labour Commissioner (Central) and the conciliation officer.

Every industrial establishment employing twenty or more workers must constitute a Grievance Redressal Committee (GRC) comprising equal numbers of employer and worker representatives, with total membership not exceeding ten.

source_refs.citation_span: page:7 / rule 6(1) – शिकायत निवारण समिति का गठन

summary: An affected person must file an application in Form-II before the relevant tribunal within one year from the date of arising of a dispute relating to trade union registration, administration, management, election of office-bearers, or denial of membership. The application may be submitted electronically, by registered post, or by speed post.

source_refs.citation_span: page:11 / Rule 8(8) — प्रभावित व्यक्ति... एक वर्ष के भीतर... प्रपत्र-II में आवेदन

summary: Before imposing any fine on an employee, the employer must submit a written intimation to the Labour Officer having jurisdiction seeking approval for the fine. The Labour Officer must give both the employee and employer an opportunity to be heard before granting or refusing approval.

Whenever an employer makes a wage deduction for absence from duty under the proviso to section 20(2), the employer must notify the Labour Officer having jurisdiction in writing within ten days of making the deduction, explaining the reason for it.

Before making a wage deduction for damage or loss, the employer must personally and in writing explain to the employee the nature of the damage or loss and how it is directly attributable to the employee's neglect or default. This explanation must be given within one month of the date of the damage or loss.

After giving the employee an opportunity to offer an explanation regarding the damage or loss, if a deduction is made, the employer must inform the employee of the deduction within fifteen days from the date of such deduction.
Employers must record the particulars of wage advance recoveries (made in installments not exceeding 50% of wages per wage period) in the register maintained in Form-I.

Where wages due to an employee remain undisbursed because no nomination was made or for any other reason, the employer must deposit all such undisbursed amounts with the jurisdictional Labour Officer before the 15th day after the last day of the six-month period, via bank transfer or crossed demand draft drawn on a Scheduled bank in favour of the Labour Officer.

source_refs.citation_span: page:14 / r.39 — Deposit of the undisbursed dues

summary: Arrange each employee's working day so that it comprises eight hours of work and rest intervals not exceeding one hour in total, and ensure no employee works continuously for more than four hours without a rest break.
Ensure that each employee's working day, including rest intervals, does not spread over more than twelve hours on any day, and that no employee works more than forty-eight hours in a week.
If employees work six days a week, arrange work so that the period of work inclusive of rest intervals does not exceed ten and a half hours per day, and ensure the seventh day is a paid holiday.

If employees work fewer than six days a week under flexible working hours, arrange work so that the period inclusive of rest intervals does not exceed twelve hours per day, and ensure the remaining days are paid holidays; obtain prior consent of the negotiating union/council or majority of employees before granting such flexibility.
Inform each employee of their designated weekly rest day and of any subsequent change to that rest day before the change takes effect, by displaying a notice at the place of employment.
Allow every employee who has worked continuously for at least six days under the same employer a weekly rest day, which shall ordinarily be Sunday unless the employer fixes another day.

Display the notice regarding fines at a conspicuous place in the workplace premises, or share it with employees in electronic form, so that every concerned employee can easily read and understand it. Send a copy of the notice to the Inspector-cum-Facilitator having jurisdiction, either physically or electronically.

Before imposing a fine on an employee, the employer must give a written intimation to the Inspector-cum-Facilitator to obtain approval for the fine. The Inspector-cum-Facilitator must provide both the employee and the employer an opportunity to be heard before granting or refusing approval.
When an employer makes a deduction from wages due to absence from duty, they must notify the Inspector-cum-Facilitator with jurisdiction within ten days of the deduction, providing reasons for it.

Before making a wage deduction for damage or loss, the employer must personally and in writing explain to the employee the nature of the damage or loss and its attribution to the employee's neglect or default, provide an opportunity for the employee to respond, and then inform the employee of the deduction within fifteen days of making it.

When recovering advances of money or unearned wages from an employee, the employer must ensure each instalment does not exceed 50% of the employee's wages in any wage period and must record the particulars of such recovery in Form-I.

Where wages remain undisbursed due to absence of nomination or any other reason, the employer must deposit all such undisbursed amounts with the Deputy Labour Commissioner before the 15th day after the last day of the six-month period, via bank transfer or crossed demand draft drawn in favour of the Deputy Labour Commissioner.
A single application under section 45(5) of the Code on Wages must be filed in Form-II along with the documents specified in that Form.
proof_types: supporting documents as specified in Form-II

summary: Any person aggrieved by an order of the authority under section 45(2) may file an appeal in Form-III, along with documents specified in that Form, to the appellate authority having jurisdiction.
proof_types: supporting documents as specified in Form-III

summary: Employers must record all fines imposed and all realizations thereof in a register maintained in Form-I (electronically or otherwise). The Deputy Labour Commissioner having jurisdiction is the designated authority for this purpose.
Employers must record all deductions made from wages and all realizations thereof in a register maintained in Form-I (electronically or otherwise).
Every employer must issue wage slips in Form-V (electronically or otherwise) to each employee on or before the payment of wages.
An accused person wishing to compound an offence under section 56(1) of the Code must submit an application in Form VI (electronically or otherwise) to the notified Gazetted Officer.
proof_types: acknowledgment of receipt by Gazetted Officer

summary: If the Gazetted Officer determines the offence is compoundable and the accused agrees, the accused must pay 50% of the maximum fine prescribed for the offence within the time specified in the composition order.
proof_types: payment receipt for 50% of maximum fine

summary: Pay revised dearness allowance to employees on minimum wages, effective from 1st April every year.

source_refs.citation_span: page:5 / r.5 — 'The revised dearness allowance so calculated, shall be payable from April 1st of every year.'

summary: Ensure the normal working day for employees consists of exactly eight hours of work with rest intervals not exceeding one hour in total.

source_refs.citation_span: page:5 / r.6(1) — 'The normal working day...shall be comprised of eight hours of work and one or more intervals of rest which in total shall not exceed one hour.'

summary: Arrange the working day so that, inclusive of rest intervals, it does not spread over more than twelve hours on any single day.

source_refs.citation_span: page:5 / r.6(2) — 'The working day of an employee shall be so arranged that inclusive of the intervals of rest...it shall not spread over more than twelve hours on any day.'

summary: Inform employees of their designated weekly rest day (and any change to it) before the change is effected, either by displaying a notice at the workplace or by prior electronic intimation.

source_refs.citation_span: page:5 / r.7(1) second proviso — 'the employee shall be informed of the day fixed as the rest day and of any subsequent change in the rest day before the change is effected, by display of a notice...or prior intimation in electronic form.'

summary: Allow every employee who has worked continuously for at least six days a full weekly rest day (ordinarily Sunday, or any other fixed day).

source_refs.citation_span: page:5 / r.7(1) — 'an employee shall be allowed a day of rest every week...if he has worked under the same employer for a continuous period of not less than six days.'

summary: Do not require or permit an employee to work on their rest day unless a substituted full rest day is provided within five days before or after the original rest day; ensure no employee works more than ten consecutive days without a rest day.

source_refs.citation_span: page:5 / r.7(2) — 'Any such employee shall not be required or allowed to work on the rest day unless he has or will have a substituted rest day for a whole day on one of the five days immediately before or after the rest day.'

summary: When a registered worker dies, the nominee must submit an application in Form VI to claim the Natural Death Assistance of Rs. 25,000, accompanied by the death certificate, Living Member Certificate from the revenue department, Aadhaar-linked bank passbook, and the original identity card (or registration number if the original is unavailable).
proof_types: original identity card or registration number

summary: Every establishment with 500 or more workers (other than those covered under section 22(1)) must constitute a Safety Committee comprising representatives of employers and workers.
In case of mines, the Safety Committee must hold meetings at least once every month.
The occupier, employer, owner, agent, or manager of an establishment must take action to implement the Safety Committee's recommendations within 15 days of receiving them.
The Safety Officer must maintain a detailed record of all work performed by them in a paged bound register/book.

Every employer at a dock work establishment employing 500 or more workers must appoint Safety Officers in the prescribed numbers based on the total dock worker headcount (1 officer for up to 1,000 workers, scaling up proportionally for larger workforces).

Every employer in building or other construction work employing 250 or more workers must appoint Safety Officers in the prescribed numbers based on total building worker headcount (1 officer for up to 500 workers, scaling up proportionally for larger workforces).

Every mine employing 100 or more persons must appoint at least one Safety Officer (one per 500 workers, plus one additional Safety Officer for each additional 500 workers or part thereof) who holds the prescribed qualifications for the type of mine (coal underground/opencast, metalliferous underground/opencast, or oil mines).
The Safety Officer must maintain detailed records of all mine accidents and analyse them to identify the nature and common causes of accidents in the mine.
Employers must issue appointment letters (in the prescribed format) to existing employees who were not already given one, within three months of this rule coming into force.

source_refs.citation_span: page:5 / r.7 proviso (three months from rule coming into force)

summary: If a fatal accident occurs at an establishment (factory, dock work, mine, building or other construction work), the employer/manager/occupier must immediately notify the Inspector-cum-Facilitator and Chief Inspector-cum-Facilitator electronically in Form VI, and also inform the District Officer or Sub-Divisional Officer, the officer in charge of the nearest police station, and the family/relatives of the deceased/injured person by telephone.

If a person injured in an accident or dangerous occurrence (already reported under sub-rules 1 and 2) subsequently dies, the employer/occupier/manager must immediately notify the authorities mentioned in sub-rules 1 and 2 by telephone and electronically, and confirm the notification in writing within 12 hours of the death.
proof_types: written confirmation of death notification within 12 hours

source_refs.citation_span: page:6 / sub-rule (3) — first proviso (death after accident/dangerous occurrence, notice within 12 hours of death)

summary: If the disability of 48 hours or more (referenced in sub-rule 2) does not arise immediately after the accident or dangerous occurrence but arises later or arises in multiple instalments, send a report in Form VI to the Inspector-cum-Facilitator within 24 hours of the total actual period of work-incapacity reaching 48 hours.

source_refs.citation_span: page:6 / sub-rule (3) — second proviso (delayed or cumulative 48-hour disability, Form-VI within 24 hours)

summary: When a dangerous occurrence (as listed in the Schedule) happens in an establishment—whether or not it causes bodily injury or disability—the employer/occupier/manager must send a notice in Form VI to the Inspector-cum-Facilitator and the District Magistrate or Sub-Divisional Officer within 12 hours of the event.
proof_types: dispatch record to District Magistrate / Sub-Divisional Officer

source_refs.citation_span: page:6 / sub-rule (3) — first paragraph (dangerous occurrence notice within 12 hours)

summary: Upon receiving information from an employee about an imminent danger to their health and safety, the employer must immediately take remedial action and send a report of the actions taken to the Inspector-cum-Facilitator electronically or by registered post or speed post.

An employer whose establishment is not already registered must apply for registration electronically via Form-I on the Shram Suvidha Portal (or nominated portal), uploading required documents such as proof of identity, address, and establishment details. The application must be digitally signed and the applicant is responsible for the accuracy of all information provided.

The registration authority must issue a digital Registration Certificate in Form-II within 7 days of a complete application being submitted; if not issued within this period, the establishment is deemed registered and a certificate is auto-generated.
The employer must display a copy of the Registration Certificate at a prominent place in the establishment's premises, either as a hard copy or electronically. The certificate is non-transferable.
proof_types: physical or electronic display of Registration Certificate (Form-II)

summary: An employer whose establishment is already registered under any other central labour law must update the registration details on the Shram Suvidha Portal (or nominated portal) within six months of the Code coming into force.
proof_types: updated registration details on Shram Suvidha Portal

summary: The employer must quote the registration number on all documents prepared or completed under the Code, Rules, Regulations, or Schemes, and in all correspondence with the concerned office.
The employer must update any change in ownership, management, or any other detail given in the registration form on the portal within 30 days of such change.

An employer dissatisfied with an order of the Registration Officer may file an appeal electronically or by registered post/speed post to the Appellate Authority appointed by the Central Government within 30 days of receipt of such order.

If an appeal is dismissed for non-appearance, the appellant may apply for restoration of the appeal to the Appellate Authority within 30 days of receipt of the dismissal order, electronically or by registered post/speed post.

Every employer of an establishment (factory, mine, contract labour, or building/construction work) must submit Form-IV electronically to the Registration Officer within 30 days of commencement or completion of work; on closure, the notification must be accompanied by a certificate that all worker dues have been paid and the premises cleared of hazardous chemicals and substances.

Every employer of an establishment must arrange free annual medical examination for each employee who has completed 40 years of age; the examination must be conducted by a qualified medical practitioner using Form-V, and a medical certificate must be issued to the employer and the employee.

The employer must notify the Inspector-cum-Facilitator having jurisdiction over the area where the establishment is located within 30 days of commencement or completion of any work, or closure of the establishment, by submitting Form-IV electronically; this information is auto-shared with EPFO and ESIC.

An employer seeking to register a beedi and cigar work establishment (not already registered) must apply electronically via Form-V on the Official Portal, uploading required documents including site plans, premises details, and proof of payment of the prescribed registration fee (via treasury challan/e-challan).
proof_types: site plan showing premises and surroundings

summary: The registering officer must issue a Certificate of Registration in Form-VI electronically within fifteen working days of receiving a complete application; if not issued within this period, registration is deemed granted and the certificate is auto-generated.

When any details in the Registration Certificate need to be changed, the employer must apply electronically via Form-V on the Official Portal, uploading amendment documents and paying the difference in fee (if any) by treasury challan/e-challan.
proof_types: treasury challan / e-challan (differential fee payment, if applicable)

summary: An employer of a building and other construction work establishment not already registered must apply electronically in Form-V on the Official Portal, providing establishment details, uploading required documents, and attaching proof of payment of the registration fee via treasury challan or e-challan. The form must be digitally signed or signed as required by the portal.
proof_types: treasury challan / e-challan (proof of registration fee payment)

summary: The registering officer must register the establishment and issue a Certificate of Registration in Form-VI electronically within fifteen working days of receiving a complete application; if not done within this period, the establishment is deemed registered and the certificate is auto-generated.

An employer must apply electronically in Form-V on the Official Portal to amend the Registration Certificate, uploading documents related to the amendment along with proof of payment of any differential fee via treasury challan or e-challan.
proof_types: treasury challan / e-challan (proof of differential fee payment)

summary: After receiving an online amendment application, the Registering Officer must verify the details and issue the amended certificate within fifteen working days.
The Chief Inspector Cum Facilitator must maintain electronically a register of Factories in Form IV, showing particulars of all factories for which a Licence has been issued.

Obtain prior written permission from the Chief Inspector Cum Facilitator before using or bringing into use any building as a factory (or part thereof), before carrying on any manufacturing process in a newly constructed, reconstructed, or extended building, or before installing additional machinery or prime movers exceeding the horsepower already installed.

Submit an application electronically in Form-I along with a fee of ₹2,000 paid online to the state treasury, accompanied by a manufacturing process flow chart, scaled plans (in PDF) of the factory site and buildings, and (for hazardous process factories) a certificate from the Karnataka State Pollution Control Board confirming arrangements for disposal of industrial liquid wastes, effluents, and air pollutants.
proof_types: Karnataka State Pollution Control Board certificate (hazardous process factories)

summary: Every employer of an establishment to which this Code applies (that came into existence after commencement) must electronically apply to the registering officer for registration of the establishment within sixty days from the date of applicability of this Code.

Every registration application must be submitted electronically in the prescribed form and manner, include particulars such as information on inter-State migrant workers, and be accompanied by the prescribed fees.

If any change occurs in the ownership, management, or any registered particulars of an establishment after registration, the employer must electronically intimate the registering officer in the prescribed form within thirty days of such change.

Within thirty days of closing an establishment, the employer must electronically inform the registering officer of the closure and certify that all dues to workers have been paid, in the prescribed manner.
